title: Microsoft Purview: improved built-in sensitive information types
summary: The roadmap facts and the documented inspection and copying controls check out. However, the guidance presents an inventory of available sensitive information types as a way to identify those used by policies; the cited command does not document that capability. The licensing field also understates published product-level licensing.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No licensing specific to the improvement is published, represented by licensing.model unknown.
claims.quote: The per-user licensing model is the familiar Microsoft 365 E3/E5/A5/F5/G5 model. It remains unchanged. This licensing model enables you to apply Microsoft Purview controls and protections to Microsoft 365 and Windows/macOS endpoint-based assets.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included and cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-billing-models. Begin the notes: 'For Microsoft 365 and Windows/macOS endpoint assets, Purview uses the Microsoft 365 E3/E5/A5/F5/G5 per-user licensing model. No licensing specific to this improvement is published.' Retain the credential-scanning qualification. The existing unknown value understates the published product-level model; the searched SIT and service-description pages do not name an improvement-specific entitlement.

claims.claim: Microsoft publishes no separate meter or charge for this improvement as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: "Purview" "improved sensitive information types" licensing meter price. Read Purview billing models, the Purview service description and SIT overview; none names a separate improvement meter.

This example lists all the properties of the sensitive information type named "Credit Card Number".
